question.text: Under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, which of the following is correct with respect to an AIF Investment Manager and its designated persons?

answer.text: PIT Regulations apply only to listed companies and their promoters; AIFs are outside scope
PIT applies only if the AIF has more than 50% holding in a listed investee company
Only the Compliance Officer of the AIF is bound by PIT; fund managers and analysts are exempt

An AIF and its designated persons can be 'deemed connected persons' due to potential access to UPSI about listed investee companies; the Board must adopt an Internal Code of Conduct, maintain a structured digital database of UPSI recipients (with PAN) preserved internally for at least 8 years, and enforce Chinese Walls and pre-clearance for designated-person trades

explanation.text: The Logic: Because an AIF Manager can have access to unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI) about listed investee companies, the AIF and its designated persons can be treated as "deemed connected persons" under the PIT framework. The Manager's board is required to adopt an Internal Code of Conduct, designate persons covered by the code, maintain a structured digital database of UPSI recipients with PAN-level identification preserved for at least 8 years, and enforce Chinese Walls between information-barriered teams along with pre-clearance for designated-person trades. The Trap: Option A wrongly excludes AIFs from the PIT perimeter; the regulations expressly contemplate intermediaries and persons with UPSI access. Option B invents a 50% shareholding trigger that does not exist in the PIT framework. Option C wrongly carves out fund managers and analysts; designated persons under the Code cover the full investment-decision chain, not only the Compliance Officer. Note: The four operational anchors to remember are: deemed-connected-person status, internal Code of Conduct, structured digital database of UPSI recipients (PAN-tagged, preserved internally for at least 8 years) and Chinese Walls plus pre-clearance for designated-person trades.
